body:
The logcat snippet doesn't include enough information to diagnose this issue.

Can you take a full bug report (`$ adb bugreport`)? It will include additional logging from before the stack trace you've snipped, as well as lots of useful info about the state of the device at the time of the problem.

If you're unable to share [bug reports](https://developer.android.com/studio/debug/bug-report) or test content publicly, please send them to dev.exoplayer@gmail.com using a subject in the format "Issue #1234" ("#1234" is replaced with your issue number). Please also update this issue to indicate you've done this.

hi, thank you for looking into this issue.
Attached is bugreport generated with `$ adb bugreport` just after playback failure.
[bugreport-sabrina_prod_stable-QTS2.200918.033-2021-03-12-07-09-52.zip](https://github.com/google/ExoPlayer/files/6130979/bugreport-sabrina_prod_stable-QTS2.200918.033-2021-03-12-07-09-52.zip)

Thanks for the BR, there's **a lot** of lines like this coming from the DRM module which are apparently errors but seem like they might actually be fine (the length varies on each line):

```
E oemcrypto_tz: [_oecc48:872] decrypt CENC data_length 223968, decrypt in chunk
```

And then right before the Java playback error stack trace there's some other errors from the DRM/Widevine components that look like the probable cause:

```
I oemcrypto_tz: [OEMCrypto_TEEInvokeData:476] cmd 1048 return 28
E oemcrypto_tz: [OEMCrypto_TEEInvokeData:478] error return 28
E oemcrypto_tz: [_oecc48:905] error return 28
E WVCdm   : Decrypt error result in session sid9 during unencrypted block: 178
```

@jt64 can you take a look from a Widevine perspective? Thanks!

Hi,
We wanted to present another observation, it might help to analyze further this bug.
While trying to resolve a problem "Buffer too small" issue on Amazon Toshiba Fire TV, we observed that 
"getCodecMaxInputSize" method in MediaCodecVideoRenderer.java gives "Format.NO_VALUE" for mime type VIDEO_DOLBY_VISION. So we added case to resolve "Buffer too small" issue as below
```
      case MimeTypes.VIDEO_DOLBY_VISION:
      case MimeTypes.VIDEO_H265:
      case MimeTypes.VIDEO_VP9:
        maxPixels = width * height;
        minCompressionRatio = 4;
```

In above code when "minCompressionRatio" is set to 2, i.e. increase Max Buffer requirement, current issue also seems to go away.

But, we could not get exact relation between Crypto Module error (Operation not supported) and buffer size.
Just providing additional info, if it helps to root cause correct issue..

Thanks for that extra detail about `MediaCodecVideoRenderer` - changing something in that method looks like a sensible improvement to ExoPlayer.

Since Dolby Vision can wrap both AVC and HEVC content, and AVC has a lower minimum compression ratio, I'm going to add it to the H264 case block instead.

I'll go ahead and make that change.

Thank you @icbaker,
But do we know why we observe error in crypto module when buffer size is not set? Also, error goes away only when compression ratio is set to 2. 

I agree that adding change at H264 block make sense. I hope same VIDEO_DOLBY_VISION MimeType is used for both AVC and HEVC codecs..

> But do we know why we observe error in crypto module when buffer size is not set? Also, error goes away only when compression ratio is set to 2.

We don't know why this happens. I think it's probably a device specific issue. We will follow up with the Sabrina team [Internal ref: b/183920895].

Hi ojw28,
     For sabrina, This issues is fixed in b/169426633, the reason is secure input buffer size  not big enough for some dv files;
